html:
The Baiyungu, also spelt Payungu, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Gascoyne coast of Western Australia, around Coral Bay and the coast inside Ningaloo Reef. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their country is a dry coast next to one of the world's great fringing reefs, rich in fish, turtle and dugong. Their neighbours were the Thalanyji to the north and the Tharrkari and Yinggarda inland and to the south. Sheep stations took up the coast from the late 1800s.
